note: 2-participant (sub-01, sub-02) demonstration that the alignment pipeline (RSA, CKA, cross-state retrieval, subject-level aggregation) runs end to end against real preprocessed data with a perception-only-trained EEGNet encoder evaluated on held-out imagery trials. sub-05 was excluded (too few surviving trials after artifact rejection, consistent with results/c1_encoder_smoke.json). This is explicitly NOT a confirmatory H3/H4 result -- 2 participants and a lightly-trained (15-epoch) encoder cannot support a transfer claim either way. It demonstrates the machinery works and reports what it found honestly rather than only on a case where the numbers looked good.

excluded_participants.sub-05: too few surviving perception/imagery trials after artifact rejection (see results/c1_encoder_smoke.json)

not_implemented: The optional frozen visual-semantic image-encoder target (e.g. CLIP) was not implemented: ds005815 does not distribute the actual stimulus images, only descriptive categories (trigger_codebook.py), and adding a large pretrained image encoder for a handful of geometric/face stimuli with no source images available was judged not worth the dependency weight for an explicitly optional component.
interpretation: Modest, mixed, and honestly reported: sub-01 shows retrieval meaningfully above its own chance level (2.4x), sub-02 shows retrieval below its own chance level (0.33x). With n=2 participants and a lightly-trained encoder, this is consistent with either a real but weak/heterogeneous transfer effect or with sampling noise -- it cannot be distinguished with this N. Per C1_PROTOCOL.md Section 6, subject-level distributions (not a pooled trial-level number) are the correct unit here, and this is exactly why H3/H4 remain exploratory pending the full participant set in a controlled research workflow, never presented as a confirmatory transfer claim from this evidence alone.
